policy_prompt_for_subgoal: An episode starts in A (pick up the container), with the point on the first entry of target_containers computed from the demonstration at that same step. Rules at any decision step: (1) If the scene shows the gripper raised with fingers partly closed (about 46% open), it is holding a container: choose B (put down the container). (2) If the fingers are fully open (about 100%) and put_down_count is less than the number of entries in target_containers, choose A and point at the container whose current listed position is nearest to target_containers[put_down_count + 1] (1-based: the first entry when put_down_count is 0, the second when it is 1); write the point as that container's listed position. (3) If the fingers are fully open and put_down_count equals the number of entries, every named container has been handled; choose A and point at the last entry of target_containers again (harmless repeat). If a situation matches none of these rules (e.g. gripper state unclear), pick the rule whose gripper description is closest: partly closed fingers mean B, open fingers mean A on the next unhandled target.

fields.name: target_containers
fields.description: Ordered list of container positions [y, x], one per cube named in the goal instruction, in the order the goal names them. Write it at the first decision step (memory empty, demonstration steps shown) by this procedure, then copy it unchanged at every later step. Procedure: (1) from the first demonstration frames note each named cube's position; (2) at the first frame listing containers, the named cube's container is the one nearest that cube; the positions listed in that frame are the slots; label the named container by its slot; (3) go through the remaining frames; whenever a frame lists two containers at positions that are not slots (off by well over 10 pixels), a shuffle is under way between the two containers whose slots are now empty; it lasts until a frame again shows all containers at slots; at that frame those two containers have SWAPPED slots, so if the named container was one of the two, its slot is now the other container's old slot; a second shuffle of the same pair swaps them back; shuffles of other pairs do not change its slot; (4) never assume a container returns to its own starting slot, and never take the container resting nearest the cube's original position in the last frame; the entry is the named container's slot after every swap, written with that slot's coordinates as listed in the last demonstration frame. Worked example: cube at [70, 119]; containers first rest at [66, 120], [84, 109], [93, 163], [119, 145]; the cube's container is [66, 120]; later frames show [66, 120] and [84, 109] both off their slots for three frames, then all back; those two swapped, so the cube's container is now the one at [84, 110] in the last frame; entry [84, 110]. e.g. [[84, 110], [93, 163]]

fields.name: put_down_count
fields.description: Number of containers picked up and then put down so far. Write 0 at the first decision step. Add one to the carried-in value when the execution steps of the current step show the fingers reopening from about 46% to about 100% after being lowered over a container (a put-down just completed); otherwise copy the carried-in value. e.g. 1
